the influence of the illumination by the diffuse light of sky on the apparent properties of the sea is very important, and it is not limited only to the blue and green parts of the spectrum.
the apparent optical properties (diffuse reflectance and diffuse light attenuation) of seawater depend on the illumination conditions and that the dependence is strong and nonlinear.
The apparent optical properties (AOP) of the sea are determined by inherent optical properties (IOP) and illumination parameters (IP) of the Sun and sky.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diffuse attenuation coefficient is not a unique property of seawater, and it is necessary to specify the source of illumination.
the diffuse attenuation coefficient is not a constant of the sea water and the sea is not a black body.

, in general, the diffuse reflectance of the sea is a nonlinear function of the diffuse attenuation coefficient, and the diffuse attenuation coefficient is a nonlinear function, in its turn, of the diffuse reflectance, and that both of them are also nonlinear functions of the inherent optical properties of the medium, the Sun and sky illumination, and the solar zenith angle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffuse light of a cloudless sky can be considered to be a source of illumination for the sea.

the influence of illumination by the direct solar beam on the apparent optical property is significant in a very narrow range of solar zenith angles and for the sea of high optical depth, i.e., the sea with high concentrations of chlorophyll.

the diffuse reflectance and the diffuse attenuation coefficient are coupled and that the apparent optical properties depend on the inherent optical properties, on the parameters of the Sun, and the sky, on the solar zenith angle, and the solar altitude.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the influence of direct illumination by the Sun on the apparent optical characteristics of the sea is much less significant than the influence of the diffuse light of sky, and that the latter can be described by using the concept of the diffuse attenuation coefficient of the sea.
the diffuse attenuation coefficient is not a function of depth alone, but also of illumination conditions.

the diffuse light of a cloudy sky is an important source of illumination of the sea and that it must be taken into consideration in the calculations of apparent optical properties of optically deep seawater.
